name: Gabor
author: E. T. Carter
description: Directional Gabor noise as a dark satin surface: a sparse convolution of oriented Gaussian-windowed cosine kernels sums into long parallel streaks that break and re-phase where the kernels overlap. The field is shaded as a low relief under a raking key light with an anisotropic sheen sweeping across the fibre direction, while the dominant orientation turns slowly and a gentle swirl combs it across the frame.

params.label: Kernel density
params.effect: Kernel cells across the frame height; low is a few broad streak clusters, high is a dense fine weave.

params.label: Stripe frequency
params.effect: Cosine cycles per kernel; low is wide soft bands, high is tight hairline streaks.

params.label: Angular spread
params.effect: Random tilt of each kernel about the dominant orientation; 0 is perfectly combed, 1 is an isotropic ripple.

params.label: Turn speed
params.effect: How fast the dominant orientation rotates; 0 holds the comb direction still while the phases keep creeping.

params.label: Relief
params.effect: Strength of the raking light and the anisotropic sheen; 0 is a flat matte print of the field.
